findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct Context/Problem item 1: `rebar remote-cert` (src/rebar/_commands/remote_cert.py, story ee0b) IS an in-repo client for POST /opcert/jobs; re-argue the 'no way to obtain a prod attestation' claim against that client's actual behaviour rather than its assumed absence.
evidence: Plan: 'no client exists in the repo. grep for opcert/jobs outside opcert_service/app.py finds only the nginx template, the terraform output description, and unit tests ... nothing in rebar does.'
search_files 'opcert/jobs' returns src/rebar/_commands/remote_cert.py:135 (POST /opcert/jobs) and :144 (GET /opcert/jobs/{job_id}) — a repo client, NOT only tests/nginx/terraform
src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:63 registers 'remote-cert' as a top-level command; docs/cli-reference.md:483 documents it; tests/unit/test_remote_cert.py exercises it
findings.finding: The plan's Context/Problem premise #1 ('no client exists in the repo' for the op-cert service; grep for opcert/jobs 'finds only the nginx template, the terraform output description, and unit tests ... nothing in rebar does') is false on the reviewed tree. `src/rebar/_commands/remote_cert.py` (story ee0b) is a registered `rebar remote-cert` CLI command that SigV4-signs and POSTs {ticket_id, kind} to /opcert/jobs and polls GET /opcert/jobs/{id}.
findings.location: Context / Problem, numbered item 1 ('no client exists in the repo')
scenarios: Any reader (or the ticket comment that repeats this premise) concludes no client exists and therefore no prod-attested path is reachable — when `rebar remote-cert <id> plan-review` is exactly that path.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'no client exists in the repo' with an accurate account: `rebar remote-cert <ticket-id> plan-review` submits to the service (SigV4) and persists the returned envelope; then state why that path is nonetheless not the chosen remedy (e.g. requires opcert_remote_url + AWS creds + prod service reachability), if that is the real argument.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct Context/Problem item 2 and the 'Explicitly out of scope ... no op-cert service client' line: `remote_cert.persist_envelope` already records the returned envelope as a ticket SIGNATURE attestation — reconcile the descoping with the existing client.
evidence: Plan: 'It returns the envelope in the job record, and there is no rebar CLI that records a returned envelope onto a ticket as its attestation.'

src/rebar/_commands/remote_cert.py:84-122 persist_envelope(): builds a record {manifest, algorithm, envelope: job['envelope'], material_fingerprint, merged_log_commit, ...} and calls append_event(resolved, 'SIGNATURE', record, ...)

remote_cert.py:5-6 docstring: 'on a PASS verdict PERSISTS the returned envelope + its bound fields as a SIGNATURE event (the SAME record shape signing.sign_opcert_manifest appends; auto-pushed with the tickets branch)'
tests/unit/test_remote_cert.py:3-6 pins 'the PERSIST contract — the returned envelope is stored as a SIGNATURE event the op-cert verifier certifies'
findings.finding: The plan's Context/Problem premise #2 ('there is no rebar CLI that records a returned envelope onto a ticket as its attestation') is false. `remote_cert.persist_envelope` does exactly this: on a PASS it appends the returned envelope + bound fields as a SIGNATURE event in the same record shape sign_opcert_manifest writes, so verify_signature / rebar verify-opcert certify it.
findings.location: Context / Problem, numbered item 2 ('there is no rebar CLI that records a returned envelope onto a ticket as its attestation')
scenarios: The plan (and the ticket's comment #1, which repeats 'never persists what it signs') treats record-back as impossible, ruling out the prod path a priori.
findings.suggested_fix: Acknowledge remote_cert.persist_envelope as the existing record-back mechanism; if the plan still declines to use the prod service, justify it on the operational grounds (service reachability / creds / policy) rather than on the non-existence of a client or a record path.

findings.finding: Deleting verify_opcert removes the ONLY ticket-id subject-binding check, so the new chain cannot classify a cross-ticket cert as 'wrong-kind' as the plan claims, and can ACCEPT a replayed cert.
findings.location: Fix plan step 1 + AC4 + Security reasoning 'What is retained' + Testing (subject-binding regressions)
findings.suggested_fix: In the new chain, after `envelope, bound = decoded`, keep a source-independent subject-binding check: if `str(bound.get('ticket_id')) != str(ticket_id)` return `{'verdict':'wrong-kind', ...}`, and if `str(bound.get('kind')) != _PLAN_REVIEW_KIND` return `{'verdict':'wrong-kind', ...}`. This reads only the SIGNED payload fields (not the plaintext mirror) and preserves subject binding without re-introducing the keyring/provenance gate. State in the plan that this replaces verify_opcert's Phase 0 binding responsibility, which compute_validity does not carry.

findings.finding: The plan asserts subject binding is retained such that 'a cert bound to another ticket ... classifies wrong-kind and BLOCKS', but the decision rule that enforced cross-TICKET binding (verify_opcert Phase 0) is deleted by Fix plan §1 and the replacement terminal step compute_validity has no co-located ticket-id binding check, so it cannot produce wrong-kind for a cross-ticket cert.
findings.location: AC4 + 'Security reasoning → What is retained' + 'Testing' (test_classify_rejects_a_cert_bound_to_another_ticket); Fix plan §1
findings.suggested_fix: In classify_plan_review_attestation, after decoding, add an explicit subject-binding gate on the SIGNED payload: if str(bound.get('ticket_id')) != str(ticket_id) or bound.get('kind') != _PLAN_REVIEW_KIND, return {'verdict': 'wrong-kind', 'reason': 'attestation is bound to a different ticket/kind'} (FLAG bucket). Then update the plan's Fix plan §1 and Testing to state this new co-located check as the enforcer of the two subject-binding regressions, rather than implying compute_validity provides it.

findings.finding: The plan's reduced attestation chain (delete `verify_opcert`, keep `opcert_from_record` -> `compute_validity`) performs NO cryptographic signature verification and NO subject-binding check, so it cannot deliver the plan's own AC4 ("does NOT let a change self-certify from an untrusted environment"). `verify_opcert` (src/rebar/attest/opcert.py:174) is the sole site that verifies the DSSE signature (Phase 1) and enforces the subject binding against replay/cross-ticket/cross-kind/mutated-material (Phase 0); `opcert_from_record` (opcert.py:336) only DECODES and its docstring states the payload is authenticated ONLY by the signature `verify_opcert` checks; `compute_validity` (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py:513) never verifies a signature — for plan-review it only rejects when `attestation['verified'] is False` (attest.py:535) and otherwise trusts caller-shaped fields. Since the tickets-branch record is documented attacker-writable and non-Gerrit-gated (opcert.py:347-351), an attacker can write any decodable envelope — or replay a cert minted for a different ticket/kind — onto the plaintext record and the reduced chain will accept it.
findings.location: Fix plan step 1 (bugfix_size_gate.py: delete the verify_opcert call + _plan_review_anchor); AC line 'whatever path is chosen does NOT let a change self-certify from an untrusted environment'
findings.suggested_fix: Keep `verify_opcert` (and its storage-anchor/`_plan_review_anchor` derivation) so the signature + subject binding are still checked; remove ONLY the trust-source gating by loading a keyring that trusts the signing principal (the pattern already committed: pinning the developer env in trusted_environments.yaml) rather than dropping verification entirely. If a signatureless design is genuinely intended, spike it first with an explicit written threat-model for the attacker-writable tickets branch.

findings.finding: The plan's foundational premise — that .rebar/trusted_environments.yaml pins exactly ONE environment (nava-opcert-prod) with 'no client' — is false on the reviewed tree: the file pins TWO environments, the second (ade0f2ef-51cc-45a2-bb97-c09846cd3df5) being the maintainer's developer gate environment added specifically to resolve this unsatisfiability (per its own comment referencing bug 846b / Gerrit 1355), and it is the principal that signed 129e's plan-review attestation.
findings.location: Context / Problem (".rebar/trusted_environments.yaml on main pins exactly ONE environment") and the plan title
findings.suggested_fix: Re-state the problem against the current .rebar/trusted_environments.yaml (two pinned envs) and explain why removing provenance gating is still warranted given a developer env is already pinnable — rather than asserting none is.
